a5-b158-b155:
Most sober people don't feel much from zeolite, but when the trip is toxic or the gut is driving it, the effect is easy to feel. I put a spoonful of zeolite into a cup of water or juice and sip slowly (some people need a teaspoon, others a tablespoon). Rubbing the zeolite on the body or just holding its jar also helps me.

In my experiments, zeolite has to be prepared correctly. I use powdered zeolite rather than nano-liquid zeolite. Many products did nothing for me, I think because most zeolites have clogged pores that haven't been cleaned, but ZeoCharge is sold as cleaned.
a5-b156-b157:
For my ozonated zeolite, I mix the powder into water and use an ozone-water purifier in a glass vessel because ozone destroys plastic. I mean ozonating water, never inhaling ozone gas. With a machine producing about two grams of ozone per hour, ten minutes produced a working zeolite for me, however much zeolite was in the water. Less time didn't work as well, and more time didn't noticeably improve the zeolite.

Zeolite binds metals, which is part of why it is used for heavy-metal removal, so I don't put it into a metal thing or use a metal spoon. I use glass for ozonating and storing it whenever I can.
a2-charcoal:
I don't treat charcoal and zeolite as interchangeable, because drugs bind to activated charcoal as well as gut toxins, so it can flatten or reduce a trip.

So if someone took too much, or the gut itself is toxic, I give charcoal. If the trip is going fine and only the gut feels bad, I give zeolite, which leaves the trip alone.

Medicines bind to charcoal too, so I'd think twice before giving it to someone who depends on one. If medics come, tell them charcoal was taken.
